A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The proofs and visualization appendices can be matched across versions, including the move of visualization Appendix E to Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original Stable Diffusion v3.5 experiments on COCO, numerical results in Tables 1–2, and generated-image comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds diversity measurements, β-guidance comparisons, and peak-timing ablation results in Table 3.

M1.justification: The proposed TV guidance procedure remains the same normalized, piecewise linear schedule over sampling steps specified in Appendix D. Calling it linear in Section 4.2 clarifies the existing method; β-guidance is added as a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-image generation using COCO and retain the same illustrative prompts. The new diversity evaluation samples within COCO, and the peak-timing study varies configurations within the existing task.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add β scheduling for both CFG and APG alongside the retained variants. Malarz et al. was already cited in v1 but was not evaluated there. Figure 4 replaces its APG panels with a β-CFG panel; quantitative APG comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a dedicated quantitative diversity protocol using 1,000 COCO prompts, 16 images per prompt, and mean squared pairwise distances between LPIPS features. It also introduces a controlled peak-timing sweep at NFE=10 and ω=7. This substantially extends evaluation of the central diversity claim; the existing quality-benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix E and Table 3 test sensitivity to guidance peaks at 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% of sampling steps. This adds one focused hyperparameter analysis; the earlier early/late-guidance tests and supplementary visualization cases are retained.

E5.justification: The new diversity evaluation explicitly specifies 16 images generated with different random seeds per prompt. This adds seed and sampling information, without establishing an increase in repeated benchmark runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All shared numerical entries in Tables 1–2 are unchanged, but β results, diversity scores across variants, and Table 3 substantially expand the empirical findings. At NFE=10 and ω=9, β-CFG has higher reported diversity than TV-CFG (1.242 versus 1.223), but lower ImageReward (0.790 versus 0.932), revealing an additional quality–diversity tradeoff.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1, Theorems 3.2, 3.3, and 3.5, Proposition 3.4, and the mathematical arguments in Appendix C are retained. Added explanations of guidance notation and the proposition's interpretation do not revise the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and stated contributions retain the same three-stage account, early/global and late/local diversity-loss claims, and practical motivation for time-varying guidance. The conclusion preserves their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 4 now emphasize the shared low-high-low principle across TV, interval, and β schedules, replacing the earlier emphasis on TV's advantage over interval guidance. Appendix E newly interprets intermediate peaks as robust, early peaks as harmful to quality, and late peaks as restricting diversity.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds β's Beta-density scheduling description, normalization and hyperparameter-source information, and LPIPS feature aggregation details. The model, image resolution, hardware, software, TV schedule formula, and code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Balaji et al. (2022) and Li et al. (2024), linking their early-shape/late-detail observations to the stage-wise account in Section 3.4. The already-cited Malarz et al. becomes an explicit scheduling comparator. The detailed theoretical related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify the perturbation experiment and Proposition 3.4's interpretation. v2 updates the publication header, adds acknowledgements, and inserts an ablation appendix before the retained visualizations. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain β and diversity rows, reorder metrics, and Table 1 loses its redundant Best columns. Figure 4 changes from six panels to four, Figure 5 adds a β curve, and Table 3 is new. Other illustrations are retained. Table 1 introduces an inconsistent downward diversity arrow despite Appendix D and Tables 2–3 specifying higher-is-better.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's largely visual diversity evidence, v2 supplies direct quantitative diversity measurements, a relevant competing schedule, and a focused peak-timing sensitivity test. These strengthen assessment of the practical claims and expose useful tradeoffs. The gains are bounded within the existing experimental scope, and the inconsistent diversity arrow in Table 1 reduces clarity, but the net effect is a supported improvement.
